title: I Ran a Shrimp Boat for 31 Years — Read This Line on the Bag Before You Buy Shrimp Again
description:
I ran a shrimp boat out of Biloxi for 31 years. Most shrimp sold as "Gulf" never saw the Gulf — and the proof is one small line on the back of the bag. Here's how to read it, where to buy real Gulf shrimp, what it should cost, and how we cook it on the coast.

Read 3 lines on any bag of raw shrimp (10 seconds):
1. The country — "Product of USA" vs. "Product of India / Ecuador / Vietnam…" (required by law on raw shrimp in grocery stores).
2. Wild caught or farm raised (also required).
3. The ingredients — it should say "shrimp" (maybe salt). If you see sodium tripolyphosphate / "to retain moisture," you're paying shrimp prices for water.

Watch out for: "Packed in…", "Gulf style", "Cajun style" (they don't tell you where it was caught), and cooked/breaded shrimp (no country label required). Sizes: trust the count per pound (16/20, 21/25), not "jumbo."

pinned_comment:
Quick version: flip the bag. Read the COUNTRY, read WILD or FARM RAISED, and read the INGREDIENTS — if it says sodium tripolyphosphate, put it back. 🦐
What does the bag in your freezer say? Country + wild or farmed.
